key_insight: X-ray absorption and DFT+U reveal that oxygen-vacancy ordering in NdBaCo2O5+δ may be more complex than expected, with vacancies likely present at both basal and apical sites and δ closer to 0.75 than 0.65.
engineering_relevance: Controlling vacancy distribution in layered cobaltates can tune magnetic inhomogeneity, charge transport, oxygen-ion mobility, and ultimately improve oxygen-sensing performance.
evidence_signal: The near-edge spectral feature count and shape across Co K, Ba LIII, and Nd LIII edges support a higher effective oxygen content (δ closer to 0.75) and confirm Ba2+ oxidation state.
watch_item: The vacancy-location and δ assignment are inferred from spectroscopic signatures and modeling, so local disorder or sample nonuniformity may limit how directly the structure can be generalized.
paper_title: X-ray absorption spectroscopic studies of oxygen-deficient double perovskite oxide NdBaCo$_2$O$_{5+δ}$ ($δ\sim 0.65$)
